2026-11-09.detail:
Easy pace for distance.
This is exactly as it says, it should feel very easy, almost too easy. These runs are used as recovery runs or pre/post a big race or challenge.

2026-11-10.title: Upper Body Strength
2026-11-10.detail:
CLICK ON VIDEO TAB FOR DEMONSTRATION OF MOVEMENT.
•Warm-Up:
• Shoulder Taps – 2 x 20 (10 per side)
• High Knees Slow – 2 x 30 seconds (alternate legs)
•Main Set:
1. Chest Fly on Floor – 3 x 10
2. Push Press – 3 x 12
3. Press-Up Negative – 3 x 10
4. Side Plank (Easy or Hard) - 45 seconds each side
5. Plank Jacks - 3 x 30 seconds
•Cool-Down:
• Foam Rolling Back – 60 seconds
• Couch Stretch – Hold 20 seconds per leg

2026-11-10.title: Ankle/Calf/Achilles Strengthening - lower impact
2026-11-10.detail:
Calf raises each leg x 20
Jump on the spot x 30
Jump on the spot each leg x 10
Jump left/right x 10 each leg
Jump forward/backwards x 10 each leg
Squat x 10
Lunge x 8 each leg
Roll calfs

2026-11-11.title: Functional Core
2026-11-11.detail:
CLICK ON VIDEO TAB FOR DEMONSTRATION OF MOVEMENT.
•Warm-Up:
• World's Greatest Stretch – 4 per side, hold 10 seconds per position
• Reverse Lunge with Knee Drive – 2 x 10 per leg
•Main Set:
1. Side Plank Hard (do Side Plank Easy if needed) – 2 x 45 seconds per side
2. Plank – 3 x 45-second hold
3. Dumbbell Under Core Move – 3 x 12 (can use any weight if you don't have a dumbbell)
4. Romanian Deadlift – 3 x 10 (dumbbells or bodyweight)
•Cool-Down:
• Soleus Stretch – Hold 30 seconds per leg
• Scorpion Stretch – 10 slow reps (5 per side)

2026-11-15.title: 20 km | Ultra pace
2026-11-15.detail:
Ultra pace (preferably on trails - walk the hills)
This is a pace to aim for during long runs when training for your ultra. This pace is will seem slow as it basically takes into account the fact that you will be both running and walking. It's essentially a 'keep moving' pace and is more aimed at stopping you going too fast than anything else.
